title: Enrolment opens the same modal from three places, offering every schedule
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in, on the build under test, as a service advisor with the view customers and create and edit customers permissions.
  2. Your organization has two workplaces (locations), e.g. "Calgary South" and "Red Deer", and your user can open both; you switch between them with the location control in the header.
  3. Two schedules exist: "Highway Tractor PM" built with "Calgary South" chosen in the header, and "Trailer PM" built with "Red Deer" chosen (switch the header location before clicking New schedule). Seed each with the standard steps (New schedule, one service, Save).
  4. An asset of a test customer (e.g. unit 402 of "Aacrest Works") with an open work order, and, if the environment has one, an asset listed under two customers.
  5. Your user also holds "Settings Service" for step 5 (archiving and restoring the schedules).
custom_steps:
1. With "Red Deer" chosen in the header, open the asset's Maintenance tab and click Enroll in Schedule; read the schedules offered and the line under each.
  2. Cancel. Open the customer's Assets tab and click Enroll in Schedule; then open the asset's work order and use enrolment from its maintenance card. Compare the three modals.
  3. On the asset listed under two customers, open the modal and read how it asks for the customer.
  4. Enrol asset 402 on "Highway Tractor PM", then open Enroll in Schedule again and look for "Highway Tractor PM".
  5. In Settings archive both schedules, open Enroll in Schedule on another asset and read the modal; afterwards restore both schedules.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Both schedules are offered whichever location is in the header, each with its home location beneath it ("Lines from Calgary South", "Lines from Red Deer").
  • All three entry points open the same modal.
  • The modal asks which customer to enrol for (it is preselected where the asset has only one customer).
  • A schedule the asset is already on is not offered.
  • With no schedules the modal says so plainly and offers a route to create one, not an empty list.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10564 (S7, Enrol an asset onto a schedule), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S7 (Where it starts; S7-R1, S7-R23, S7-E8, S7-N6); Plan 1 — Track, act, clear — Technical Implementation Plan, section 3.3 Frontend decisions, FD-23; read 6 Oct 2026.
